items.q: Why are viruses not considered living organisms?
items.qAf: Hoekom word virusse nie as lewende organismes beskou nie?
options: They have no cells and cannot reproduce alone
optionsAf: Hulle het geen selle en kan nie alleen voortplant nie
items.explain: Viruses are non-cellular and need a host cell to replicate.
items.explainAf: Virusse is nie-sellulêr en het ’n gasheersel nodig om te repliseer.

items.q: Bacteria are classified as prokaryotes because they:
items.qAf: Bakterieë word as prokariote geklassifiseer omdat hulle:
items.explainAf: Prokariote het geen membraangebonde kern nie.

items.q: Antibiotics are effective against bacteria but not viruses because:
items.qAf: Antibiotika is effektief teen bakterieë maar nie virusse nie omdat:
options: viruses have no cell structure for antibiotics to target
optionsAf: virusse geen selstruktuur het wat antibiotika kan teiken nie
items.explain: Antibiotics target bacterial cell processes, which viruses do not have.
items.explainAf: Antibiotika teiken bakteriële selprosesse, wat virusse nie het nie.

items.q: Fungal cell walls are made of:
items.explain: Fungi have chitin cell walls, unlike plants, which have cellulose.
items.explainAf: Swamme het chitien-selwande, anders as plante, wat sellulose het.

items.q: Which group includes unicellular eukaryotes such as Amoeba?
items.qAf: Watter groep sluit eensellige eukariote soos Amoeba in?
items.explain: Protists are mostly unicellular eukaryotes, and Amoeba is one example.
items.explainAf: Protiste is meestal eensellige eukariote, en Amoeba is een voorbeeld.

items.q: Yeast is useful in baking because it:
items.qAf: Gis is nuttig in bak omdat dit:
options: Produces carbon dioxide that makes dough rise
optionsAf: Koolstofdioksied produseer wat deeg laat rys
items.explain: Yeast ferments sugars, releasing CO₂ gas that gives bread its rise.
items.explainAf: Gis gisting van suikers, en stel CO₂-gas vry wat brood laat rys.

items.q: The thread-like structures that make up the body of a fungus.
items.qAf: Die draadagtige strukture waaruit die liggaam van ’n swam bestaan.

items.q: A mutually beneficial association between a fungus and plant roots.
items.qAf: ’n Wedersyds voordelige verbintenis tussen ’n swam en plantwortels.

items.text: HIV attacks the body's [[]] cells, which weakens the immune system. The disease it causes in its final stage is called [[]].
items.textAf: MIV val die liggaam se [[]]-selle aan, wat die immuunstelsel verswak. Die siekte wat dit in sy finale stadium veroorsaak, word [[]] genoem.

items.explain: False. Viruses are not cells: they are a protein coat around DNA or RNA.
items.explainAf: Onwaar. Virusse is nie selle nie: hulle is ’n proteïenmantel om DNS of RNS.

items.q: Tuberculosis (TB) is caused by a bacterium.
items.explain: True. TB is caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis and is treated with antibiotics.
items.explainAf: Waar. TB word deur Mycobacterium tuberculosis veroorsaak en word met antibiotika behandel.

items.q: Match each disease in column A with the type of micro-organism that causes it in column B.
items.qAf: Pas elke siekte in kolom A by die soort mikro-organisme wat dit veroorsaak in kolom B.

items.q: Explain why antibiotic resistance is a growing problem, and give ONE way to slow it down.
items.qAf: Verduidelik waarom antibiotikaweerstand ’n groeiende probleem is, en gee EEN manier om dit te vertraag.
points: When antibiotics are overused or the course is not finished, resistant bacteria survive and multiply.
Slow it by finishing the full course / only using antibiotics for bacterial infections when prescribed.
pointsAf: Wanneer antibiotika oorgebruik word of die kursus nie voltooi word nie, oorleef weerstandige bakterieë en vermeerder.
Vertraag dit deur die volle kursus te voltooi / antibiotika net vir bakteriese infeksies te gebruik wanneer dit voorgeskryf is.
